description: Excalidraw itself is not something Renovate can track, and no annotation in defaults/main.yml pretends otherwise. `excalidraw/excalidraw` on Docker Hub carries one usable tag, `latest`, beside a set of `sha-*` tags abandoned in 2021; the image has no version label of its own; and the self-build path this role takes by default compiles the `master` branch. `excalidraw_version: latest` is the honest description of that, which is also why the version component of this repository's tags is a date somebody picked rather than anything derived from upstream.

What Renovate does track here is `excalidraw_container_image_self_build_base_image_tag`: the Static Web Server release that the self-built image serves the compiled application from. Patch bumps of it are automerged; minor and major bumps remain pull requests for a human, which matters because Static Web Server 3.x is already published as a beta and changes configuration semantics this role depends on.

Patch automerge is safe for this dependency in a way it is not for most: Static Web Server is a static file server with no state whatsoever. It is a single binary as the image's entrypoint, this role mounts no volume into it, and the systemd unit runs it with a read-only root filesystem and no added capabilities. There is no database, no schema and no migration that a patch release could run unattended on restart - the class of risk that keeps automerge off elsewhere in this fleet does not exist here.

The automerge branch is covered by the `default-selfbuild` Molecule scenario, which builds the image against the bumped base and then makes the running process account for itself. Static Web Server announces its version, its bound port, its document root, its fallback page and its log level on startup, and the scenario reads all of that back out of the journal and compares it against what the role's own templates were told to render. It cross-checks the version against the image's `org.opencontainers.image.version` label and its `SERVER_VERSION` environment variable, both of which were confirmed to move with the release across 2.42.0, 2.43.0 and 2.44.0 rather than reporting some base image's number. It then fetches the compiled bundle and requires it to arrive as JavaScript, with a deliberately absent asset asserted to come back as the `text/html` fallback page so that the content-type check is known to discriminate. A patch bump that broke startup, the port binding, the fallback page or the content types fails there before it can merge.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation is what keeps that decision quiet. Of the 434 tags joseluisq/static-web-server publishes, strict semver leaves the 93 plain X.Y.Z releases: the 168 flavoured tags (`-alpine`, `-debian`, `-fips`, `-fips-alpine`, `-fips-debian`) parse as prereleases and are skipped as unstable along with `3.0.0-beta.1`, while the 66 floating majors and minors (`2`, `2.44`) and the six word tags (`latest`, `alpine`, `debian`, `devel`, `devel-alpine`, `devel-debian`) are not versions at all. Before this pin existed, templates/Dockerfile.j2 said `joseluisq/static-web-server:latest`, which Renovate skips outright - so a Static Web Server major release would have arrived on the operator's next image build, unannounced and untested.

What the suite cannot see, and what a reviewer of a red build should keep in mind: nothing here executes any JavaScript, so a bundle that is served correctly and misbehaves in a browser would pass. And because the self-build compiles Excalidraw's unpinned `master`, a failure on an automerge branch may belong to upstream rather than to the bump. That direction fails closed and blocks the merge, which is the right way round.
